name: Bedrock_DeFi
rootCause: The cause of this vulnerability is that the exchange ratio of WETH and uniBTC was not properly handled, resulting in WETH and uniBTC being exchanged at 1:1, and the value of WETH was magnified tens of thousands of times. The attacker used the distorted price to make a profit through lending, and eventually the attacker used the borrowed WETH to empty the project’s uniBTC tokens. descriptions.text: Swap ETH/BTC 1/1 in mint function. Lost: 27.83925883 BTC (~$1.7M USD)

Bedrock just got a lesson in why you should always double-check your math homework. In a twist that would make even a quantum physicist's head spin, their uniBTC vault decided to play fast and loose with exchange rates, turning Ethereum deposits into a $2m Bitcoin bonanza.

The cause of this vulnerability is that the exchange ratio of WETH and uniBTC was not properly handled, resulting in WETH and uniBTC being exchanged at 1:1, and the value of WETH was magnified tens of thousands of times. The attacker used the distorted price to make a profit through lending, and eventually the attacker used the borrowed WETH to empty the project’s uniBTC tokens. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x725f0d65340c859e0f64e72ca8260220c526c3e0ccde530004160809f6177940 Analysis: https://lunaray.medium.com/bedrock-unibtc-hack-analysis-7808902e5a7c

The multi-chain liquidity re-staking protocol Bedrock announced on social media that the team is aware of a security vulnerability involving uniBTC, with the total estimated loss from the theft around $2 million. According to the SlowMist security team’s analysis, the attack was caused by Bedrock mistakenly supporting the minting of uniBTC at a 1:1 exchange rate with the native token.

Bedrock’s uniBTC protocol was exploited on Ethereum on Sept. 26, 2024 after a flaw in the SigmaSupplier and vault minting logic allowed uniBTC to be minted using unsupported native-token paths. The attacker minted 30.8 uniBTC and swapped the tokens through liquidity pools, extracting roughly $2 million before Bedrock paused the affected contracts. The uniBTC minting system incorrectly handled native-token accounting on non-native BTC chains. Bedrock’s post-mortem stated that the SigmaSupplier contract returned a zero total supply for unregistered NATIVE_BTC assets, which caused vault cap checks to pass even though native-token minting should have been disallowed.…
